newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Lithuania signs 1997 deal with Gazprom.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania signs 1997 deal with Gazprom.

text.p: Lithuania on Friday signed a deal with Russia's Gazprom for three billion cubic metres of gas in 1997, company officials said.

Lithuanian Gas will buy 560 million cubic metres, an intermediary company Stella Vitae 1.8 billion cubic metres and huge chemicals firm Achema 640 million cubic metres for $78, $74 and just over $78 respectively per 1,000 cubic metres.
"This amount fully satisfies the needs of the country," Lithuanian Gas commercial director Vidmantas Cepukonis told Reuters after the deal was signed.
Lithuanian Gas faced big difficulties paying for the gas and had to take a $20 million credit from Union Banque Suisse.

Lithuanian Gas is in its turn owed some $21 million by the country's energy sector. The new contract says that Gazprom can cut the supply to Lithuania if payment for gas which has been supplied is delayed for two months.
Gazprom board member Alexander Pushkin said that the group would in the future like to supply some six billion cubic metres to Lithuania.
He also said that the company was interested in a possible privatisation of Lithuanian Gas.
"We would like to buy shares in the gas sector in Lithuania but that will depend on the decisions of the Lithuanian government," Pushkin told journalists.
Lithuanian Gas has so far not been on the privatisaion list but the new right-wing government of Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius wants to speed selloffs of state industries.
